title: WCAG contrast ratios
description: WCAG defines contrast as a ratio from 1:1 to 21:1, computed from relative luminance: 4.5:1 for normal text (AA), 3:1 for large text and UI components. The formula weights green heavily (human vision does). Every text/background pair in the theme is checked against these numbers — by tooling, not eyeballing. AAA (7:1) is the high-contrast target.
mechanism: L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B (linearized). Ratio = (L1 + 0.05)/(L2 + 0.05). Check every token pair in CI; fail the build on violations.
algo: O(pairs) checks; trivial compute, total coverage.

title: Theme tokens
description: Theme tokens name colors by purpose, not appearance: --text-primary, --surface-overlay, --border-focus — never --light-gray. Every theme (light, dark, high-contrast) provides values for every token; components only reference tokens. Adding a theme means filling the token table, not touching components. The token set is the contract between design and code.
mechanism: Token table per theme; components use tokens only; no raw colors in components. Token additions are additive (old themes get defaults). Lint bans raw colors.
algo: O(tokens) per theme; components O(1) lookup.

title: Dark mode
description: Dark mode is a full theme, not an inversion: surfaces go dark, text goes light, but accent colors shift (blue #0066cc becomes #66aaff for contrast on dark), shadows become glows, and images get dimmed overlays. Elevation inverts (lighter = higher). Auto-switch follows the OS; the toggle is per-app; the choice persists. Test both — half the users live in dark.
mechanism: Separate token table; prefers-color-scheme media query; manual override stored. Accent ramps designed per mode (not auto-inverted). Images: brightness filter.
algo: O(1) switch; the work is designing the dark ramp.
demo:
# dark mode: designed ramp, not inversion
light = {'surface': '#ffffff', 'text': '#1a1a1a', 'accent': '#0066cc', 'shadow': 'dark'}
dark = {'surface': '#121212', 'text': '#e8e8e8', 'accent': '#7ab8ff', 'shadow': 'glow'}
print('light:', light)
print('dark :', dark)
print('accent SHIFTED (#0066cc -> #7ab8ff): contrast on dark, not naive invert')
print('elevation inverts: lighter = higher; images get dimmed overlays')

title: Forced colors mode
description: Forced colors mode (Windows High Contrast) is the OS taking over: it replaces the page's colors with the user's system palette, and the site must respect it. CSS: use forced-color-adjust carefully, system color keywords (CanvasText, ButtonFace), and never convey meaning by color alone here. Test with the mode on — it breaks every custom-styled control that assumes its colors survive.
mechanism: @media (forced-colors: active): use system colors; forced-color-adjust: none only where essential (with a non-color fallback). All meaning duplicated in text/icons, not color.
algo: O(1); the work is auditing every custom control.
demo:
print('FORCED COLORS (Windows High Contrast) RULES')
print('@media (forced-colors: active) {')
print('  .btn { background: ButtonFace; color: ButtonText;')
print('          border: 1px solid ButtonText; }  /* system colors */')
print('}')
print('forced-color-adjust: none -- ONLY where essential, + non-color fallback')
print('meaning NEVER by color alone: text + icon always')
print('test with the mode ON: it breaks every control that assumes its colors')

title: Focus indicators
description: Focus indicators show keyboard users where they are: a visible outline on the focused element, always. The styles are 2px+ solid outlines with offset (so they show on any background), never removed without replacement. :focus-visible shows the ring for keyboard but not mouse click. In high contrast, the indicator uses the system highlight color. Invisible focus = unusable by keyboard.
mechanism: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }. Never outline: none without a replacement. Forced-colors: use Highlight system color.
algo: O(1); the discipline is never removing it.
demo:
print(':focus-visible {')
print('  outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring);')
print('  outline-offset: 2px;  /* visible on ANY background */')
print('}')
print('RULES: never `outline: none` without a replacement ring;')
print(':focus-visible (keyboard) not :focus (mouse click);')
print('forced-colors: outline-color: Highlight (system)')
print('invisible focus = keyboard users are lost')

title: Color blindness
description: Color-blind-safe design never encodes meaning in red/green alone: 8% of men have red-green deficiency. The fixes are redundant encoding (color + icon + text), palettes chosen for distinguishability (ColorBrewer, Okabe-Ito), and simulators to verify. Charts get patterns/labels, not just hues. Test with a simulator — your eyes lie about what others see.
mechanism: Okabe-Ito palette (colorblind-safe); redundant encoding everywhere; simulate deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia in CI screenshots. Never red/green as the only signal.

print('8% of men: design for them from the start, not as a fix')

title: Theming engines
description: Theming engines apply themes at runtime: CSS variables for the web (swap the token table, everything repaints), resource dictionaries for native, and user stylesheets for power users. The engine handles transitions (no flash of unstyled), persistence, and per-surface overrides. Dynamic themes (Material You's wallpaper colors) generate the token table algorithmically.
mechanism: Web: :root variable swap + transition. Native: resource dictionary swap. Dynamic: seed color -> tonal palettes (Material You algorithm). Persist choice; respect OS default.

title: CSS variables for theming
description: CSS custom properties are the web's theming engine: define tokens on :root, override per [data-theme], and every component inherits. The cascade does the work — theme switching is a single attribute change. Fallbacks (var(--x, default)) keep old components working. Scoped overrides theme subtrees (a dark dialog in a light app).
demo:
print(':root { --bg: #ffffff; --text: #1a1a1a; }')
print('[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #121212; --text: #f0f0f0; }')
print('[data-theme="hc"]   { --bg: #000000; --text: #ffffff; }')
print('.card { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }')
print('')
print("document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'dark'  // ONE attribute")
print('cascade propagates; var(--x, fallback) keeps old components alive')

title: OS theme integration
description: Apps follow the OS theme: prefers-color-scheme on web, trait collections on iOS, uiMode on Android. The app listens for changes (the user flips at sunset) and switches live. The stored preference has three states: light, dark, system — 'system' is the default. Per-app override exists for users who differ from the OS.
mechanism: Match the OS signal; three-state preference (light/dark/system); live-update on OS change events. Respect it on first launch (no flash of wrong theme).

print('Android: Configuration.uiMode + recreate on change')
print('preference: light | dark | system (default: system)')
print('rules: follow on first launch (no wrong-theme flash); switch LIVE on OS change')

title: Testing contrast
description: Contrast testing is automated: every token pair checked in CI (axe-core, custom scripts), screenshots diffed per theme, and manual testing with real low-vision users. The pipeline fails on violations — contrast is a build gate, not a suggestion. Dynamic content (user colors, charts) gets runtime checks with fallbacks.
mechanism: CI: token-pair matrix x themes -> ratio checks -> fail on <4.5 (text). Screenshot diff per theme. Runtime: check user-chosen colors, adjust if failing.
algo: O(pairs x themes) in CI; runtime O(1) per user color.

title: User theme preferences
description: Theme preference is a first-class setting: light/dark/system, plus high-contrast as a separate axis (a user can want dark AND high contrast). It syncs across devices, applies before first paint (no flash), and respects the OS reduce-motion/transparency companions. The setting is easy to find — buried theme settings help no one.
mechanism: Preference = {mode: light|dark|system, contrast: standard|high}. Apply pre-paint (inline script / native early). Sync via account. High contrast independent of dark mode.
demo:
prefs = {'mode': 'system', 'contrast': 'high'}  # independent axes!

def effective(os_dark):
    mode = os_dark if prefs['mode'] == 'system' else (prefs['mode'] == 'dark')
    theme = 'dark' if mode else 'light'
    if prefs['contrast'] == 'high':
        theme += '-hc'
    return theme

print('OS dark + HC pref ->', effective(True))
print('OS light + HC pref ->', effective(False), '(dark AND high-contrast are separate)')
print('apply pre-paint: inline script reads prefs before first render')

title: Documenting themes
description: Themes are documented like APIs: the token table with values per theme, usage rules per token (when to use text-primary vs text-muted), contrast ratios achieved, and do/don't examples. Documentation is what lets 50 engineers theme consistently. The docs are generated from the token source — never hand-maintained separately.
mechanism: Token source (JSON/YAML) -> docs site generator -> token tables, swatches, ratios, examples. Lint the docs build for missing tokens.
algo: O(tokens) generation; docs never drift from source.

title: Migrating to theme tokens
description: Migrating a codebase to tokens is mechanical: codemod raw colors to the nearest token, add missing tokens for the gaps, then flip themes on and fix what looks wrong. The codemod maps hex values to tokens (fuzzy match); humans review the ambiguous ones. Migrate incrementally — one surface at a time, both themes working throughout. The lint ban on raw colors lands last, when the migration is done.
mechanism: 1. Codemod hex->token (fuzzy). 2. Human review of ambiguous. 3. Per-surface migration. 4. Lint ban on raw colors. Both themes green throughout.

title: Theme performance
description: Theme switching must be instant: CSS variable swaps repaint without reflow (color-only changes are cheap), but theme changes that alter layout (spacing, fonts) cost more. Keep themes to color/elevation tokens; avoid per-theme layout changes. Preload all theme token tables (they are tiny). Measure the switch — users flip at sunset and notice jank.
mechanism: Color-only tokens (compositor-friendly); single attribute switch; no layout-affecting theme values. Measure switch time; budget <100ms.

print('THEME SWITCH PERF')
print('cheap: color/background/border-color (repaint only)')
print('expensive: spacing/fonts/layout per theme (reflow: avoid)')
print('rule: themes = COLOR + ELEVATION tokens; layout never theme-dependent')
print('preload all token tables (tiny); one attribute switch; budget <100ms')
print('users flip at sunset: they WILL notice jank')

title: Theme tooling
description: Theme tooling keeps the system honest: token linters (no raw colors, no undefined tokens), contrast checkers in CI, theme preview switchers in dev, and screenshot diffing per theme. The toolchain runs on every commit — a PR that breaks dark mode contrast fails before review. Tooling is what makes 'themeable' a property of the codebase rather than a hope.
mechanism: Lint (stylelint custom rules) -> contrast CI -> visual regression per theme -> dev preview switcher. All blocking in CI.
algo: O(codebase) lint; O(screens x themes) visual.
demo:
print('THEME TOOLCHAIN (all blocking in CI)')
print('1. lint: no raw colors, no undefined tokens (stylelint rules)')
print('2. contrast: every pair x every theme >= 4.5:1 (axe)')
print('3. visual: screenshot diff per theme (Chromatic)')
print('4. dev: one-click theme switcher in the dev server')
